prospect.name: Hariharan Ramanarayanan
prospect.location: United States, Pacific time zone; originally from India
prospect.occupation: Technology — data privacy, working specifically on youth privacy. In the office three days a week, working from home the rest. Employer provides on-site food.
prospect.family_status: Married. One son, two and a half years old, born in December, just starting school at roughly $24,000 a year. Wife is starting a small business. Only child; sends money to his parents in India each month.
prospect.training_background: Played soccer through high school and college. Was lean and healthy until COVID, after which his health 'took a nosedive'. Since then a repeating cycle: gym-based personal training about two years ago and high-intensity interval training, both abandoned — HIIT at six to seven sessions a week of 45-60 minutes left him depleted within two to three weeks. About a month before this call he bought a Bowflex adjustable kettlebell for home and began following Trevor's YouTube workouts, 25-30 minutes a day, and reports visible change within a week with no nutrition changes at all. Walks 8-10k steps a day, largely with his toddler at the park. Practises 18-20 hour daily fasts with a four to six hour eating window.
prospect.medical: Chronic lower back and trapezius stiffness and pain, attributed to sitting all day, historically from 8am to 1am. Historic low back injury from playing soccer at school and college, which he characterises as not a fracture and not a spinal injury. Reports that a week and a half of kettlebell swings noticeably improved his glutes and lower back. Recent blood work clear, including magnesium and vitamins. Sleeps 10:30-11pm for seven to eight hours, occasionally six with a toddler, but wakes tired. Vegetarian, eats eggs only outside the home because his wife has an airborne egg allergy that makes her nauseous from the smell. No other conditions disclosed.

signals: Explicit loss of a former self to a defined bad season: 'I used to be quite lean and healthy a few years back. And then since probably COVID after that happened, it has taken a nosedive with regards to my personal health.'

Wants the old body back rather than a new one — 'by end of December I'm actually back to where I have ever been in my life' and 'I just want to feel like I'm back in my 20s and not like a 35, 36-year-old dad'.
Carries visible regret about repeated failed attempts: 'this fitness thing has been one of the goals for me every single year for the past two, three years.'
Not the_optimizer: he describes the current state as a decline to be reversed, not a good baseline to be improved.
Distinct from the_preserver: he is 34 and the frame is comeback, not maintenance.

objections.rep_response: Paused and let it land — 'Take a breath. You good?' — then reframed rather than defended: 'It's a big step, but it's a good step. You know that, yeah?'

objections.rep_response: Isolated first, asked permission to have the financial conversation, then ran a full open wallet — monthly surplus, savings, investments and credit cards with limits — before proposing two structures: half down plus three monthly instalments of $1,000, or Pava financing spread up to twelve months.

objections.raw_quote: Can I get maybe an hour or two? We are just crunching some numbers. Okay. yeah, I'll for sure, like, I'm completely on board. I just want to actually crunch some numbers to figure out.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Two structures proposed, both preserving the $6,000 total: (a) $3,000 down followed by three monthly instalments of $1,000; (b) Pava third-party financing on a credit card, spread up to twelve months at 'a few hundred dollars each month'. The prospect chose (a) and then counter-proposed $2,000 down followed by four monthly instalments of $1,000. The rep said 'Probably, yeah. We could even split it in a different way. I'll just need to ask my supervisor.'

prospect_financials.note: Monthly surplus $1,000-$1,500 gross of remittances, about $1,000 after sending money to his parents in India, against $24,000 a year in school fees. Savings described as five figures. Some crypto, 'not much'. Credit cards with $60,000-$70,000 of total limits. Wants to protect the emergency fund, which is why he preferred instalments over drawing down savings.

evidence: No payment taken and no payment link sent, so the verbal-agreement-plus-link rule does not apply.
Very strong verbal position after he spoke to his wife: 'I'll for sure, like, I'm completely on board. I just want to actually crunch some numbers to figure out.'
He negotiated the instalment structure himself rather than the price, which is buying behaviour: 'Is it possible to do 2K and four months 1K, if that's an option?'
The terms he asked for were not confirmed — the rep said he would have to check with his supervisor.
A same-day follow-up was booked at a specific time, 2:30pm Pacific on the same Zoom link.

Counter-evidence: he had expected a price of $2,000-$3,000, was audibly shocked at $6,000 ('That's quite a lot. Wow. I did not expect this'), and the household has competing commitments in the next two to three months including his wife launching a business.
outcome.next_step: Reconvene at 2:30pm Pacific the same day on the same Zoom link, with the prospect and his wife having finalised the numbers and the rep having cleared a $2,000-plus-four-times-$1,000 structure with his supervisor.

notable.note: The best-executed call in the batch and the model for the money conversation specifically. The rep isolated the objection, asked permission to talk about finances, then ran the full open wallet in order — monthly surplus, savings, investments, number of credit cards and available limits — and only then proposed structures, all of which preserved the $6,000 total. No invented tier, no discount, no scope cut. He also handled the spouse objection by muting, turning off his video and waiting on the line while the prospect went upstairs to talk to his wife, which produced 'I'm completely on board' seventeen minutes later. Two things still need flagging. He told the prospect the six-month programme would deliver his target by 1 December, which is five months from a 4 July start, against a stated goal date the prospect had set for his son's birthday. And a historic low back injury plus current chronic lower back pain went into a loaded ballistic hinging programme with no question about clinical clearance — the rep instead affirmed that the swings had already helped.

quality.notes: The first forty minutes are usable with frequent short-turn inversions. From roughly 00:34:00 the transcript collapses: speaker labels stop being emitted almost entirely and the whole price presentation, the open wallet and the spouse conversation run as one unbroken block attributed to Hariharan Ramanarayanan, with both voices interleaved mid-sentence. Every quote from that section was attributed by content. There is also a seventeen-minute silent gap from 00:51:36 to 01:08:40 while the prospect left the room to speak with his wife and the recording continued. The recording is otherwise complete and ends on a normal sign-off.
